cards.title: Introduction to the Factory Pattern
cards.content:
In Flask, the Application Factory pattern is a design pattern where you define a function (the factory) responsible for creating and configuring the Flask application instance.

def create_app(config_name):
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config.from_object(config_name)
    return app

cards.title: Why use Application Factory in Flask?

options.text: It makes the code run faster by caching routes.
It allows creating multiple instances of the app with different configurations, easing testing and deployment.
It is strictly required by Python to run Flask.

cards.title: Structuring the Factory Function
cards.content:
A typical factory setup initializes extensions outside the factory function without an app, and then binds them inside using init_app().

from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

db = SQLAlchemy()

def create_app(config_filename):
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config.from_pyfile(config_filename)
    
    db.init_app(app)
    
    return app

cards.title: Registering Blueprints
cards.content:
Blueprints are registered inside the factory function to modularize your application.

def create_app(config_name):
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config.from_object(config_name)
    
    from .auth import auth_bp
    app.register_blueprint(auth_bp, url_prefix='/auth')
    
    return app
